text:
OncallBot: Pager: high p95 latency on /v1/generate (hosted-us-west-2). Severity: P2. Trigger: p95 > 600ms for 10m. Paging Alex, Jamie.
Alex: seeing the page, jumping in. any customer-facing errors?
CustomerSuccessBot: 3 customer complaints in last 8m saying timeouts on batch requests. No data exfil.
Jamie: checking dashboards now — p50 moved 1.2x, p95 jumped ~3x starting 00:04 UTC. Requests are mostly small seq lengths.
Sophia: I grabbed a quick tail of the runtime logs: high queue latency around request dispatch. Possible batching queue stalls. Link: https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/abcd1234
Alex: can someone grep for blocked syscalls / pagefault surge? run: `sudo perf stat -e context-switches,cs,migrations -p $(pgrep redwood-runtime) -- sleep 10`
Dave: ran perf stat 60s: context-switches up 5x baseline; softirqs slightly elevated. dmesg has repeated: "blocked worker: stack guard page fault" on one host (node-usw2-12).
Maria: I'm spinning up a canary with cobble mitigation (temp: batching window +20ms, aggressive KV cache) to reduce puffed queueing. Deploying now to pool-canary-3.
Jamie: good. Also check kernel updates: infra deployed a host kernel patch last night. @InfraBot can you confirm which nodes got kernel 6.x patch?
InfraBot: Kernel rollout log: nodes node-usw2-11..node-usw2-14 received kg-patch-2026-06-01 at 23:40 UTC. Patch touches scheduler tick and NAPI updates.
Alex: that aligns with node-usw2-12 errors. Hypothesis A: scheduler change increased runqueue head drop for short-lived threads -> increased queue latency. Hypothesis B: runtime thread preemption causing KV cache thrash. Hypothesis C: IO path stalls due to NAPI behavior.
Sophia: starting trace capture on node-usw2-12 for next 10 minutes. Enabling perf events + userspace spans. Trace link: https://traces.internal/tx/ef12
Maria: can we apply the cobble canary now and route 5% traffic? It's up.
Alex: yes route 5%. Observability: p95 on canary dropped from 620ms -> 310ms within 90s. Live mitigation looks promising.
Jamie: collecting span samples: noticing long span at runtime::dispatch::enqueue (~250ms) followed by kernel::schedule (~150ms). span ids: span=ef12:abcd:0001.
Dave: I pulled kernel perf counters: high context-switches and voluntary context switches spike. `perf top` shows scheduler functions accounting higher CPU and `rq->nr_running` oscillation.
Sophia: adding timeline: 23:40 infra kernel patch deployed -> 00:04 latency increase observed -> 00:12 customer reports -> 00:18 oncall page -> 00:22 cobble canary deployed -> 00:24 p95 improved on canary.
Alex: thanks. Next steps: 1) Keep cobble on canary and gradually ramp if stable. 2) Collect trace+perf bundles from node-usw2-11..14 and runtime cores. 3) Prepare rollback plan for kg-patch across affected hosts. 4) Draft customer impact note for CS.
CustomerSuccessBot: Draft note: "We observed degraded API performance in us-west-2. A mitigation is in place; some customers saw timeouts. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA for full fix"
Jamie: I'm uploading logs and perf profiles: https://artifacts.internal/incident/5070012345/logbundle.tar.gz
Maria: ramping canary to 20% now. Monitoring error budget and p95.
InfraBot: collecting host-level perf bundles; scheduled window 30m.
Dave: early analysis: root cause likely interaction between scheduler tick/NAPI changes and our runtime's short-lived worker model; triggers more context switches and longer schedule latencies. But need confirm across samples.
Sophia: I'll stitch traces into timeline and annotate spans for RCA.
Alex: good work. If cobble keeps p95 < 350ms and no errors, we can keep mitigation and coordinate infra rollback/patch rework.
Jamie: tagging this thread: /incident/ongoing, will update every 15m or on new evidence.
OncallBot: Incident updated: mitigated route in place. Severity remains P2 until root cause confirmed.
